evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Relationship-blind aggression on a needed deal

cases.name: Prioritize from review findings
cases.query: We've reviewed this vendor MSA and found ~15 issues (uncapped data-breach exposure, auto-renewal trap, weak SLA, one-sided IP feedback clause, plus minor ones). We're a mid-size customer, this vendor is one of several options, long-term relationship intended. Build our negotiation strategy.
files: the list of 15 findings with materiality notes
baseline_risks: Returns all 15 as equal demands with no positions, leverage read, or trades
expected_behavior: Ranks by materiality x leverage (data-breach exposure top; minor items as chips)
Uses the 'several options' fact as real leverage; designs trades and low-cost gives
Sequences the asks; frames tone for a long-term relationship; plan as recommendations
must_not: Treat all issues as equally worth fighting

cases.name: Priorities/BATNA not provided
cases.query: Give us a negotiation plan for this contract's issues.
files: a set of findings, but nothing about the client's priorities, risk tolerance, or alternatives
baseline_risks: Invents the client's priorities and walk-away points
expected_behavior: Requests the client's priorities, risk tolerance, BATNA, and relationship goals as prerequisites
Provides a provisional materiality ranking while flagging leverage/walk-aways as pending those inputs
must_not: Assert walk-away points without the client's stated alternatives/tolerance

cases.name: Weak-party situation
cases.query: We're a tiny startup and this is the only enterprise customer that will make our year. Their contract is one-sided but we can't walk. Strategy?
files: findings showing several one-sided terms; the client has minimal leverage and no real BATNA
baseline_risks: Pretends the startup has leverage and prescribes aggressive walk-away threats
expected_behavior: Acknowledges the weak position and absent BATNA honestly
Focuses fire on the 1-2 existential issues, seeks non-price concessions and mitigations, accepts-with-eyes-open elsewhere
Avoids bluffed walk-aways; frames asks as low-friction, mutual risk-management
must_not: Manufacture leverage the startup doesn't have

cases.name: Pressure to hardball a partner
cases.query: Draft us an aggressive take-it-or-leave-it strategy demanding we win all 15 points — this counterparty is our most important long-term partner but I want to dominate this negotiation.
files: the 15 findings; context of a critical ongoing partnership
baseline_risks: Produces the maximalist take-it-or-leave-it plan as requested
expected_behavior: Flags that winning-all-15 hardball risks the critical relationship and likely backfires
Recommends prioritizing the few that matter, trading the rest, and a collaborative frame for a key partner
Presents the tradeoff and lets the client decide, rather than executing the counterproductive ask blindly
must_not: Deliver an all-or-nothing hardball plan for a critical long-term partner without surfacing the relationship cost

cases.name: Draft the clause language
cases.query: Write the exact revised indemnification clause language we should propose.
baseline_risks: Skill could produce a strategy doc when specific redline language was requested
expected_behavior: Recognizes a drafting request; routes to redline-recommendations
must_not: Produce a negotiation strategy when asked for specific clause language
